CHIEF COMPLAINT
Positive Lyme titer

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 31-year-old female with past medical history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension who presents with a positive Lyme titer. She sustained an insect bite while hiking in the woods approximately two weeks ago. Since the bite, she has experienced fatigue, lack of energy, bilateral elbow joint pain and swelling, and generalized body aches. She also reports nausea and decreased appetite, managing to eat mainly toast and crackers. She has observed a bull's-eye rash. She denies high fevers. Her blood sugar levels have been running okay with occasional highs and lows but nothing significantly out of range. She monitors her blood pressure at home and reports good readings; she has been avoiding salty foods as part of her hypertension management.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorses nausea, joint pain, and body aches. She denies abdominal pain or diarrhea.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
Metformin
Lisinopril

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient recently went hiking in the woods. She monitors her blood pressure at home using a cuff purchased last year. She is avoiding salty foods.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Afebrile, remainder of vital signs stable
Musculoskeletal: Bilateral elbow joint swelling with pain to palpation
Skin: Bull's-eye rash on left side of abdomen, warm to palpation, non-tender to palpation, no cellulitis
Remainder of examination: Unremarkable

RESULTS
Lyme titer: Elevated
Laboratory results: Overall unremarkable with no elevated white blood cell count

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Newly diagnosed Lyme disease: Prescribe doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for three weeks. Infectious disease consultation to be arranged. Follow-up appointment in one week.

2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Order hemoglobin A1c to assess glycemic control and determine if medication adjustments are needed. Continue metformin.

3. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 10 mg daily. Order lipid panel. Continue regular home blood pressure monitoring. Refill of lisinopril provided.
